approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from the current objective session’s scored observations. It keeps every accepted observation for learning, retains the best sixty-four breeding molecules, and draws parents from score quantiles for connected-fragment crossover and seven atom, bond and ring mutation families. Its inherited aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange channel is disabled. Stable canonical admission rejects duplicates, and a narrow sulfur rule rejects only new outside-envelope local signatures or increased multiplicity relative to the maximum across the original scored generating parents. Bounded refill produces a fresh pool sixteen times the announced batch size. A Gaussian process fitted to all chronological accepted labels uses chirality-aware Morgan occurrence counts and dot-product Tanimoto similarity. It normalizes raw scores using the current archive mean and population standard deviation, then allocates evaluations by correlated residual draws added to its predictive mean, with sequential exclusion of already selected pool members. Accepted feedback immediately updates the learning archive and greedy breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove repeated-environment count information only from the conditional covariance that shapes the sampled residuals. Keep the original count model’s predictive mean exactly active, and compute a second, otherwise identical GP from presence indicators of the same cached count rows. Its full conditional covariance supplies the residual factor, using the original score scale and single normal array. The earlier full-binary sibling changed both prediction mean and residual geometry; the mean-only and independent-residual siblings removed other allocation principles. This fixed consumer removal asks whether repetition-sensitive residual geometry helps productive exploration when the count-based location remains active. It is separate from the parallel binary-location probe, and the result will describe this conditional adaptive contrast.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-1744a1494180 has complete actual summary.json/run.log pairs for the issued three-seed panel: macro mean 0.59645311428869, population SD 0.03397032998399878, and seed macros 0.643098123844866/0.563172834083287/0.583088384937917. Its analysis records only 648 strict best-parent-beating offspring and 255 sequential incumbent improvements among 4350 accepted offspring, despite 3763 departures from the available posterior-mean maximizer. Thus the limiting behavior is that stochastic allocation frequently changes the chosen molecule without reliably delivering productive improvement. The evidence does not yet identify which count-information consumer supports the useful departures. The same-Parent all-output binary removal n-b9f2c3328d4c naturally exposed repeated counts in 68333/69600 pool rows, changed 434/435 same-state batch sets, and lost complete mean 0.038794771343121; its seed changes were -0.08614960727939203, +0.005329208758406034 and -0.03556391550837701, so the adverse result was heterogeneous. On its actual accepted identities, passive count predictions had MSE 0.01064970444500328 versus binary 0.01807337282750195 and mean within-batch rank correlation 0.6139505379962231 versus 0.3892570168696008, but both means and covariance changed together. Earlier ungated count removal n-e00db808bbb4 lost 0.051295849138213355 under its own Parent. Current residual-presence removal n-f04cec6ab705 and correlation removal n-8df0bb3bbcfe lost 0.11631688199011732 and 0.05054466462284635; the earlier correlation removal n-54adc6a641e8 lost 0.018447481386582327. These measured presence findings remain scoped to their literal source conditions, and the frozen catalog marks several interpretations stale. They motivate retaining nonzero correlated residual allocation while isolating count information at its covariance consumer. The inherited deco_hop seed-0 jump at evaluation 281 from 0.609560453893309 to 0.8561477222467935 remains part of the primary comparison. No preceding result settles this residual-only contribution or identifies a mean/covariance mediator.

literature_review.conclusion: Fresh primary theory, official model/code releases and the inspected Parent support constructing two exact same-archive GP systems and consuming only binary conditional residual covariance with the retained count location. I infer that removing repetition sensitivity changes residual competition among related offspring, so naturally changed choices can reach accepted feedback, later fits and breeding. Prior full-binary and residual/correlation presence losses motivate a predicted material removal loss, but do not determine this consumer-specific sign. The full exposed matched panel decides the bounded contribution criterion; passive calibration/geometry cannot establish mediation. Published count preprocessing, optimized kernels, approximations and external methods are outside this fixed probe. No external implementation, model weight, asset or dependency is needed. The recorded n-b9f2c3328d4c review was read as background; this status is searched because the primary sources were freshly read.

finding_summary.headline: Count-sensitive residual geometry contributes to endpoints even with count prediction means retained
finding_summary.insights: Count information has positive conditional endpoint value at this residual-covariance boundary even when the count-based predictive location is retained at each actual state. That narrows the earlier full-binary result: an endpoint loss does not require replacing the count mean. It does not measure how much of the earlier all-output loss was mediated by mean versus covariance, and it cannot be added to the parallel location probe. Binary residual geometry produced wider uncertainty on the selected molecules and more new generic-core parent winners, yet delivered smaller gain magnitudes and worse final endpoints. On the Child’s actual labels, count means were also more accurate and better ordered than passive binary means. Wider coverage, novelty and additional local wins therefore do not establish productive exploration. The Molecular review found recognizable amides and amines alongside more direct N-halogen attachments and more very large molecules; geometry and stereochemical identity remain unresolved. Those observations describe uneven chemical coverage, not a chemical cause of the covariance loss or evidence that a blanket filter would help. Shared Parent histories and seeds remain dependent controls. Natural failure-route robustness, separate variance/correlation mediation, sulfur interaction and transfer beyond this frozen panel remain open; final-batch sources without later fits or breeding are explicitly censored.
finding_summary.results: The covariance removal reached real search: repeated counts occurred in 68,485 of 69,600 generated pool rows, all 435 ordered selections changed against the passive count law, and 431 batch sets changed. It selected 1,590 accepted molecules absent from the passive count-selected sets; 1,538 entered later fits and 774 were later drawn as scored parents. The saved prediction means remained exactly the original count means on every selected identity. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.59645 to 0.55929, a loss of 0.03716 beyond the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.07507, +0.00262 and -0.03903; nine task-seed endpoints fell and six rose. Task means fell for zaleplon, deco_hop and sitagliptin, while median_2 rose by 0.00860 and drd2 by 0.00041. The Parent’s late deco_hop seed-0 jump from 0.60956 to 0.85615 remains in the complete comparison; omitting that cell only as a sensitivity check still leaves a mean loss of 0.02207. Strict parent wins increased from 648 to 666, but their total positive gain fell from 17.25 to 14.41. Sequential incumbent wins also rose slightly, from 255 to 258, while their total gain fell from 5.82 to 5.26. All tasks completed with the original budget, batching and dependency lock, with no natural numerical fallback.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides, linked heterocycles and aryl amines are abundant; reactive attachments and unresolved ring geometry persist
molecular.overall_character: Node n-b77e5493be1e produces indole/azaaryl amides, repeated fused nitrogen-carbonyl systems, linked oxygen/nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-bearing aliphatic amines, medium-ring nitrogen dicarbonyl frameworks and fluorinated imino/dione systems. All 15 Child and 15 published n-1744a1494180 Parent trajectory paths were present and read in full. Each side has 4500 records, including 4350 accepted optimizer observations and 150 initial records; each objective has 870 optimizer observations across Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. No task, path or paired seed is missing. context.comparison reports child_complete=true, paired_complete=true and no profile-mismatched seeds. All 15 complete Child sessions differ from their corresponding Parent records after common initial history; none is an additional identical replay. The inherited shared Parent and seed panel remain dependent controls. Published Parent chemistry is authoritative; its late seed-0 breakthrough is retained below. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not all seed incumbents. Digest ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9839-0.9954 and aromatic-string incidence 0.977-0.992. These are molecule-level text incidences, not ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. Read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 perception of every supplied SMILES finds no parse failure, median optimizer size 29 heavy atoms, four rings and three aromatic rings. Distinct seed families support moderate overall diversity, with much narrower leading series within sessions; rich rings do not establish broad plausible scaffold coverage. Synthetic plausibility remains questionable and drug-likeness weak overall because familiar medicinal frameworks coexist with N/O-halogen bonds, sulfur-halogen attachments, dense closures, small-ring unsaturation and unspecified stereochemistry. Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 1047 Child optimizer observations versus 786 Parent observations; sulfur occurs in 1381 versus 1100. The generator also emits comparatively conventional high-scoring amides and free aliphatic amines, so none of those liabilities is universally required. All digest charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0. Neutral strings nonetheless contain potentially basic amines; RDKit flags unassigned centres in 2376 Child optimizer observations versus 2455 Parent observations, with no assigned centres. Perceived centres and aromatic labels establish connectivity, not stable configurations or accessible conformations. Observed fragmentation is less frequent than in Parent, with 36 versus 82 optimizer observations of at most three heavy atoms, while elaboration above 50 heavy atoms increases to 212 versus 46. Neither change establishes chemical progress. No synthesis, 3D geometry, protonation, tautomer populations, biological activity or new oracle labels were assessed. Every complete SMILES in cited_smiles is a Child digest or trusted Child trajectory identity. Sizes and motif counts are derived directly from these trajectories and documented with path hashes in .slots/L01-resume-20261003/r32-slot3-molecular/trajectory_chemistry_audit.json. The five recurring gaps retain provenance in the original n-c55c3d520a2c report, carried through the same-code n-62daf219c70a profile baseline and the sulfur-gated n-1744a1494180 Parent. Those published reports were read through the supplied evidence_index; the older same-code baseline explicitly lacked a profile-matched Parent pairing and supplies no independent efficacy comparison here. Current re-observation is conditional on the issued three-seed, batch-ten, 300-observation-per-objective profile, inherited sulfur-relative admission and generation, and the registered count-location plus full binary-support residual law. Output associations do not decide activation or contribution, identify a covariance-mediated chemical cause, attribute a liability to m-000000000003, or establish additivity, factorial interaction, whole-foundation contribution or transfer to L07 or other starting states.

per_task.generated_character: All three seed leaders have 26 heavy atoms and three perceived aromatic rings. Seed 0 gives a vinyl/methyl/methoxy indole-like fused system with a pyridyl amide and N-fluoromethyl substituent, without a direct N/O-halogen bond. Seed 1 favors the closely related indole/pyridyl amide with aryl chlorine, ring N-F and amide N-Cl. Seed 2 retains an N-H indole/anilide framework with amide N-F or N-Cl and an N-S-methyl substituent. Median optimizer size is 25 heavy atoms versus Parent 24. The aromatic/carbonyl organization is recognizable medicinal chemistry, but the direct N-halogen and sulfenamide variants make routine synthesis and stability uncertain. Sulfur-containing observations increase from Parent 251 to Child 430 of 870.
liabilities: N-F and N-Cl bonds to ring or amide nitrogen recur in leaders; a familiar amide framework does not certify those attached environments.
N-S-methyl substitution and N-fluoromethyl groups need local assessment; sulfur-relative admission is not evidence of whole-molecule stability or synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Plausible independent realizations of the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented among leaders; 40 of the 50 highest Child optimizer observations still carry direct N-halogen bonds. The seed-0 leader is a counterexample to requiring them.

A score-effective conventional substitute for each reactive local environment is not established. The trajectories do not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore or prove that a general substitution filter would help.

Seed 1 reaches 0.4447444158980597 with N-F/N-Cl; its N-H amide relative retaining ring N-F scores 0.4387992465191. The seed-2 N-F and N-Cl amide variants both score 0.3957609793331631, while its late ordinary N-H amide/aryl chloride version scores 0.3589400387570429. These are local associations, not a general reward for reactive halogen bonds. OF and other tiny fragments score 0.0, and a 47-heavy-atom elaborated aromatic amide scores 4.970129253274748e-17. The visible gradient favors compact complete aromatic/carbonyl arrangements rather than aromatic mass or halogen presence alone. Matched Parent Top-1 values for seeds 0, 1 and 2 are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.4369542269692598. The Parent seed-0 halogen-free azaaryl N-hydroxy amide and seed-2 non-N-halogen thiocarbonyl/carbonyl leader show different ways to preserve that organization; the Child does not recover their labels on this panel.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader has 35 heavy atoms, five perceived six-membered rings and four aromatic rings. It links two fused O/N-containing carbonyl regions through NH and carries methoxy, methyl and a cyclic imine with a chloroethyl N substituent. Its recognizable heterocyclic pieces are comparatively conventional, although configuration and stability of the imine/chloroalkyl region remain unverified. Seed 0 instead builds repeated N-rich dione units: its leader has 55 heavy atoms, seven rings and six carbonyls, with an N-bromo imine and a small closure. Seed 2 has a 30-heavy-atom fluorinated aryl/tetralin-like framework with geminal diamines, allylthio and CH2-S-F substitution. Median optimizer size is 35 versus Parent 31 heavy atoms; 197 of 870 Child observations exceed 50 heavy atoms versus Parent 20, including 156 in Child seed 0. These are distinct families, not global scaffold collapse.
liabilities: Repeated fused dione regions can produce very large polyheterocycles without matching compact leaders; distinct ring-rich strings are not evidence of useful chemical coverage.
N-bromo imine, O-Br, S-F and geminal diamine environments raise local reactivity or stability questions that the sulfur-relative rule and labels do not resolve.
The seed-0 leader has a four-membered closure with unsaturation; its graph representation does not establish accessible geometry.
missing_features: Consistent compact, plausible alternatives to repeated dione concatenation are missing from the seed-0 leading series. The more compact linked seed-1 series shows that this capability is possible elsewhere in the same task-agnostic generator.

Stable local alternatives preserving the useful linked heterocyclic arrangement are not established for S-F, O-Br or geminal-diamine environments. The stronger Parent also retains reactive groups, so no unseen exact target motif follows from this record.
Stereochemical and conformational identity is unresolved where the substituted imine and saturated ring frameworks require it.

The linked seed-1 leader reaches 0.6440118031945603, with several linked carbonyl relatives at 0.6414581066376497. An O-Br-bearing relative scores 0.6412017982650542, so high labels alone do not screen out reactive attachments. The 55-heavy-atom seed-0 leader reaches only 0.6077389254966091, and its 108-heavy-atom concatenation scores 0.5713735275769697. The seed-2 S-F/geminal-diamine family reaches 0.614230202331502. The Child seed-1 improvement therefore coexists with adverse comparisons in the other seeds and does not demonstrate uniformly better feasibility.

per_task.generated_character: High-scoring output already contains available aliphatic amine centres. The seed-1 leader is a 30-heavy-atom diaryl N-methyl seven-membered azepane bearing ethoxy, aryl F/Cl, phenylthiol and terminal chloropropyl substitution. Seed 0 uses a 27-heavy-atom flexible secondary amine between two fluoroaryl regions, one fused to a four-membered carbocycle with an exocyclic alkene and alcohol, the other bearing phenol. Seed 2 gives a 28-heavy-atom dense bridged aryl/aminal framework with an N-methyl nitrogen ring and N-bromomethyl substituent; seven rings are perceived, including small closures. The cyclic amine/aryl organization is recognizable, especially in seed 1, but crowded closures, thiol/haloalkyl environments and unspecified configuration limit a general synthesis judgement. Median optimizer size is 30 versus Parent 29 heavy atoms; sulfur appears in 566 versus 254 of 870 observations.
liabilities: The leading azepane carries thiol and terminal chloroalkyl substituents; seed 2 carries N-bromomethyl and an aminal environment. Their stability and reactivity need environment-specific assessment.
Dense bridges and small ring closures coexist with attractive labels, while tetrahedral stereochemical identity remains unspecified.
The lack of charge markers is not evidence that these free aliphatic amines cannot protonate; protonation and conformational populations were not measured.
missing_features: Defined configurations and demonstrated conformations of high-scoring aryl/cyclic amines are missing: 45 of the 50 highest Child optimizer observations have unassigned centres. Basic nitrogen itself is already present despite neutral SMILES.

Conventional peripheral alternatives to haloalkyl, thiol and crowded aminal/bridge environments are not consistently represented at the strongest labels; no specific missing receptor pharmacophore can be inferred from these observations.

per_task.generated_character: Leaders combine aromatic regions, N-methyl nitrogen rings and two carbonyls, with propyl and ethoxy substitution. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
